content:
oncall-bot: Pager — P0: GPU capacity exhaustion detected in prod/us-west-2.

oncall-bot: Symptoms: request queue for `text-gen-prod` > 2k, rate limiter engaged, 95th token latency x6, autoscaler attempted 3x and hit max-scale limit.

alex: acknowledging. I see a flurry of Pending pods and a bunch of fragmented MIG allocation failures in the scheduler logs.

tia: tagging in for handoff in 15. any customer-facing impact yet?

sre-jen: CS reported ~6 customers seeing 503s/429s for embeddings and generation. Maria from CS is in the loop.

customer-success-maria: Confirmed — a few enterprise tenants seeing queued requests and elevated errors. They're asking for ETA.

alex: root signals: autoscaler can't find contiguous GPU slices for new pods because nodes have mixed MIG profiles. We have stranded GPUs: lots of small-MIG apps and a set of fat-MIG allocations blocking binpacking.

mlops-raj: that matches the model rollout yesterday — we deployed a 48GB model variant on some pools (1xA100-40) and smaller 10GB MIG workloads landed on others. Scheduler is rejecting placement due to strict MIG affinity and `prefer-binpack: true`.

eng-runtime-sam: checking scheduler events. here's a sample:

```
Evictable=false, InsufficientGPU: requested 1x40G, available fragmented: [1x10G, 1x10G, 1x20G]
FailedPreFilter: MIG profile mismatch
```

alex: autoscaler also bumped into our configured scale cap for the region: `max_nodes=120`. We hit it during the spike; scaler kept retrying but couldn't place the pods. Queue kept growing.

tia: mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily raise regional max_nodes to 140, 2) triage low-priority workloads and cordon + drain a few small-MIG nodes to free contiguous capacity, 3) create fallback route to smaller model variant (gen-small) for non-enterprise traffic. thoughts?

mlops-raj: agree on fallback. For node adjustments we should avoid mass reboots — do manual cordon/drain on 3 nodes that are mostly small-MIG consumers. I'll run a quick affinity query to find candidates.

alex: while raj finds nodes, I'm going to disable strict MIG affinity enforcement for 10m on the scheduler to allow temporary mixed placements (we have a flag `sched.allow-mig-relax`). This will let a few pods start while we rebalance.

eng-runtime-sam: caution — relaxing MIG rules can change performance characteristics. Recommend enabling it only for specific node selectors used by text-gen-prod and setting TTL.

alex: will use `--allow-mig-relax=true --mig-relax-ttl=600`. applying now.

(2m later)

oncall-bot: Action log: `sched.allow-mig-relax` toggled ON by alex.

mlops-raj: found three candidate nodes: node-uw2-078 (mostly small-MIG pods), node-uw2-115, node-uw2-201. I'll cordon node-078 and drain low-priority pods now.

mlops-raj: draining node-078 — evicting batch/spot pods. `kubectl drain node-uw2-078 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`

alex: autoscaler detected freed capacity and started provisioning placements. queue length dropping from 2100 -> 800.

customer-success-maria: relaying to customers: intermittent errors/latency; mitigation in progress; ETA ~20–30m. They'll escalate if not resolved.

sre-jen: tracking metrics: token throughput back to ~70% of baseline. still seeing some 429s for enterprise tenants pinned to the fat-MIG pool.

eng-runtime-sam: suggestion — do we want to temporarily move enterprise workloads to a different node pool or adjust their model variant? Might require config push.

alex: for minimal blast radius: create a small canary route for enterprise tenants to `gen-large` (slightly smaller) and throttle non-critical background requests. Patching routing policy now.

(10m later)

mlops-raj: drained node-115 as well. two nodes drained and re-packed. Observed several pods scheduled into newly freed contiguous GPUs.

alex: relax flag TTL expired; reverting `sched.allow-mig-relax=false`. removing temporary relaxation.

oncall-bot: Action log: `sched.allow-mig-relax` toggled OFF by alex.

mlops-raj: queue length fell to ~120. 429s mostly resolved. Enterprise tenants still at elevated latency but no errors.

customer-success-maria: customers updated — calming but asking for RCA and prevention plan.

tia: I'm taking the rest of the incident. alex / raj / sam keep me posted on any re-escalation. I'll coordinate postmortem and comms.

tia: next steps (short-term):
- confirm autoscaler `max_nodes` delta and evaluate increasing default cap with cost owner approval.
- add automation to detect MIG fragmentation and trigger proactive rebalancing before scale hits cap.
- add routing fallback for high-volume tenants so they can switch to smaller variant automatically.

sre-jen: please capture exact timestamps of hits and add relevant graphs (queue length, scale events, MIG profile occupancy). I'll open a postmortem ticket.

alex: logged actions + commands run in the incident tracker. Will attach scheduler logs and `kubectl describe` outputs.

customer-success-maria: I'm prepping a customer-facing note for affected tenants — will share draft in #customer-notifications.

tia: handing off to night oncall — please monitor autoscaler errors and queue > 200. pager policy stays P0 until fully stabilized.

oncall-bot: Handoff — incident routed to Tia, night shift.

(incident state: mitigation successful, monitoring for recurrence. postmortem required.)

Notes / commands run:
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep uw2`
- `kubectl drain node-uw2-078 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/flags?sched.allow-mig-relax=true`
- `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, reason: .status.conditions[-1]}'`

Tags: :rotating_light: P0, MIG-fragmentation, autoscale, customer-impact, handoff

End of thread.
